items.name: NdvFallback
items.summary: Fallback to use when NDV overlap can not be estimated from column bounds.

items.name: Precision
items.signature: enum Precision<T: Debug + Clone + PartialEq + Eq + PartialOrd>
items.summary: Represents a value with a degree of certainty. `Precision` is used to propagate information the precision of statistical values.

methods.name: add
methods.summary: Calculates the sum of two (possibly inexact) [`ScalarValue`] values, conservatively propagating exactness information. If one of the input values is [`Precision::Absent`], the result is `Absent` too.

methods.name: add_for_sum
methods.summary: SUM-style addition with integer widening to match SQL `SUM` return types for smaller integral inputs.

methods.name: cast_to
methods.summary: Casts the value to the given data type, propagating exactness information.

methods.name: cast_to_sum_type
methods.summary: Casts integer values to the wider SQL `SUM` return type.

methods.name: get_value
methods.summary: If we have some value (exact or inexact), it returns that value. Otherwise, it returns `None`.

methods.name: is_exact
methods.summary: Returns `Some(true)` if we have an exact value, `Some(false)` if we have an inexact value, and `None` if there is no value.

methods.name: map
methods.signature: fn map<U, F>(self, f: F) -> Precision<U> where F: Fn(T) -> U, U: Debug + Clone + PartialEq + Eq + PartialOrd
methods.summary: Transform the value in this [`Precision`] object, if one exists, using the given function. Preserves the exactness state.

methods.name: max
methods.summary: Returns the maximum of two (possibly inexact) values, conservatively propagating exactness information. If one of the input values is [`Precision::Absent`], the result is `Absent` too.

methods.name: min
methods.summary: Returns the minimum of two (possibly inexact) values, conservatively propagating exactness information. If one of the input values is [`Precision::Absent`], the result is `Absent` too.

methods.name: multiply
methods.summary: Calculates the multiplication of two (possibly inexact) [`ScalarValue`] values, conservatively propagating exactness information. If one of the input values is [`Precision::Absent`], the result is `Absent` too.

methods.name: sub
methods.summary: Calculates the difference of two (possibly inexact) [`ScalarValue`] values, conservatively propagating exactness information. If one of the input values is [`Precision::Absent`], the result is `Absent` too.

methods.name: to_inexact
methods.summary: Demotes the precision state from exact to inexact (if present).

methods.name: with_estimated_selectivity
methods.summary: Return the estimate of applying a filter with estimated selectivity `selectivity` to this Precision. A selectivity of `1.0` means that all rows are selected. A selectivity of `0.5` means half the rows are selected. An exact zero is preserv…

items.name: estimate_ndv_with_overlap
items.signature: fn estimate_ndv_with_overlap(left: &ColumnStatistics, right: &ColumnStatistics, ndv_left: usize, ndv_right: usize) -> Option<usize>
items.summary: Estimates the combined number of distinct values (NDV) when merging two column statistics, using range overlap to avoid double-counting shared values.

items.name: ColumnStatistics
items.summary: Statistics for a column within a relation

methods.name: is_singleton
methods.summary: Column contains a single non null value (e.g constant).

methods.name: new_unknown
methods.summary: Returns a [`ColumnStatistics`] instance having all [`Precision::Absent`] parameters.

methods.name: to_inexact
methods.summary: If the exactness of a [`ColumnStatistics`] instance is lost, this function relaxes the exactness of all information by converting them [`Precision::Inexact`].

methods.name: with_byte_size
methods.summary: Set the scan byte size This should initially be set to the total size of the column.

methods.name: with_distinct_count
methods.summary: Set the distinct count

methods.name: with_max_value
methods.summary: Set the max value

methods.name: with_min_value
methods.summary: Set the min value

methods.name: with_null_count
methods.summary: Set the null count

methods.name: with_sum_value
methods.summary: Set the sum value

items.name: Statistics
items.summary: Statistics for a relation Fields are optional and can be inexact because the sources sometimes provide approximate estimates for performance reasons and the transformations output are not always predictable.

methods.name: add_column_statistics
methods.summary: Add a column to the column statistics

methods.name: calculate_total_byte_size
methods.summary: Calculates `total_byte_size` based on the schema and `num_rows`. If any of the columns has non-primitive width, or `num_rows` is unknown, the previous `total_byte_size` is kept but downgraded to inexact rather than discarded.

methods.name: new_unknown
methods.summary: Returns a [`Statistics`] instance for the given schema by assigning unknown statistics to each column in the schema.

methods.name: project
methods.signature: fn project(self, projection: Option<&impl AsRef<[usize]>>) -> Self
methods.summary: Project the statistics to the given column indices.

methods.name: to_inexact
methods.summary: If the exactness of a [`Statistics`] instance is lost, this function relaxes the exactness of all information by converting them [`Precision::Inexact`].

methods.name: try_merge_iter
methods.signature: fn try_merge_iter<'a, I>(items: I, schema: &Schema) -> Result<Statistics> where I: IntoIterator<Item = &'a Statistics>
methods.summary: Summarize zero or more statistics into a single `Statistics` instance.

methods.name: try_merge_iter_with_ndv_fallback
methods.signature: fn try_merge_iter_with_ndv_fallback<'a, I>(items: I, schema: &Schema, ndv_fallback: NdvFallback) -> Result<Statistics> where I: IntoIterator<Item = &'a Statistics>
methods.summary: Same as [`Statistics::try_merge_iter`], but lets callers choose the fallback used when `distinct_count` overlap can not be estimated.

methods.name: unknown_column
methods.summary: Returns an unbounded `ColumnStatistics` for each field in the schema.

methods.name: with_fetch
methods.signature: fn with_fetch(self, fetch: Option<usize>, skip: usize, n_partitions: usize) -> Result<Self>
methods.summary: Calculates the statistics after applying `fetch` and `skip` operations.

methods.summary: Set the number of rows

methods.name: with_total_byte_size
methods.summary: Set the total size, in bytes
